utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case Number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before re-examination, there is a matter that the Registry assistant raised with the Trial Chamber before we came into the courtroom regarding the map that was discussed with the witness by Mr. Pantelic. We wanted to be clear on record, we gave it a number as an identified document only so that it's not produced, it's not part of the evidence. Is that satisfactory, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's satisfactory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. The other point is that the witness did make markings, but then there is no key as to what represents what, so we were wondering whether we can go through that again and so that he marks one represents this, two represents this, three and four and five, even though it's not being produced as part of the record, because in the event of an appeal, and the Appeals Chamber may want to look at it so it be clear, it must make sense. So perhaps you can go through that again, the document -- the map will be given to the witness and then you can ask him to mark 1, 2, whatever, so that it makes sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I absolutely concur with your approach. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Witness answered through interpreter Further cross-examined by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hadzijusufovic, let us deal with this as best we can. You made a circle around the area of Grebnice, didn't you? If you will please look at the map, this ellipse here. Just put number 1 on the Grebnice area.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why would I mark this as Grebnice? Because Grebnice stretches upwards, as far as I know. The map is rather unintelligible. I would prefer to make a drawing for you indicating the spot where I worked. Anyway, it's not a problem. I'll make a circle around whatever you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Witness, we are not reviewing the evidence you gave yesterday or the markings of that map. We just want to complete it as it is for whatever it's worth. So you are being asked to make markings by the Prosecutor -- to place numbers so that it makes sense with the record. So you are not being asked to redraw anything; it's just putting one where you placed whatever circle according to the direction of the counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzijusufovic, put number 1 to mark Grebnice, number 2 to mark Lijeskovac, number 3 to mark Brvnik, and number 4 on the line that you drew in this area above Grebnice marking Tursinovac. Put number 4 there.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay, for the records, Your Honours, the witness marked with number 1 a place called the name Grebnice. With number 2, place Lijeskovac. With number 3, place Brvnik. And with number 4, place Tursinovac, which is the bank of the Sava River.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. That's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's okay now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So it remains numbered for identification only.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we proceed with re-examination by Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Re-examined by Mr. Weiner:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, some questions were asked concerning your being convicted and sentenced to one year. For what were you convicted, as best you know?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I learned, it was a violation of the borders of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever notified of any charges being brought against you, any official notification, sir?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever served with a complaint?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Advised of any rights?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Provided counsel or told to obtain counsel?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever appear at any hearing or at any trial?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any official notice of any judgment or a sentence?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you notified of any right to appeal?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go on to some other matters which were raised in the past few days. Do you know a man by the name of Sveto Vaskonic? Did I pronounce the name Sveto?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vasovic. I do know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you known Sveto Vasovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since he moved to Samac, for about 15 years or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what, if any, relationship did you have with him? Were you friends, neighbours? What relationship, sir?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were friends from the football club. We would talk when we ran into each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you indicated to counsel that you went to see him some ten times about getting exchanged. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he tell you when you asked him on all those occasions? How did he respond to you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He will put my name on the list. That's all he can do. And Miroslav Tadic is the one who decides about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was his office located, sir, in relation to the defendant Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you go up the stairs, Miroslav Tadic's office is straight ahead; and on the right-hand side next to it is Sveto Vasovic's office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Sveto Vasovic tell you who was in charge of the exchanges?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did he tell you was in charge, sir?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on to your exchange. Now, you said when questioned by Defence counsel that you were the first off the bus or the first in line. Could you explain that, please. Is that, sir? You were the --

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you the first off the bus or the first in line?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I knew from speaking to the people who were coming from exchanges in Dubica and elsewhere that if the opposite side, or if one of the sides, had extra people who didn't want to be exchanged, then it could happen that some people on the other side do not get exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you wanted to ensure that you would become exchanged. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the occasion of your exchange, was anyone prevented from being exchanged on that -- at that time?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were told so when we arrived there. A man came to address us and said that the exchange was successful, but that two persons remained and were not exchanged. Two persons stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say two persons, two persons from what area stayed behind?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those two men were supposed to cross over together with me, to cross over the line into Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there a reason why they weren't exchanged?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't tell us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on, sir. You were also questioned by counsel concerning your being forced to loot homes in the Odzak area and what happened to that furniture. They asked you about the furniture which went to Dubica. All those items, the furniture, the appliances, the electrical equipment that was looted and that was brought to Bosanski Samac, do you know the people who received that furniture and all those other items?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these refugees from other areas?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would just ask my learned friend from the Prosecution to clarify which of the Defence counsel had asked these questions, because in redirect, questions may be asked only in reference to the questions that had been asked in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And also another matter, Your Honours. I think the term "looting" is not appropriate for the use in this examination. I mean, that's a rather legal question. So I kindly ask our friend from the Prosecution to adjust this term, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it may be too much to ask Prosecution counsel to always point out which Defence counsel raised the question, because the record is clear. And if you follow the transcript and you find that actually in cross-examination nobody raised that, then you are entitled to raise it with the Trial Chamber. But that particularization is not necessary. And on the use of the word "looting," Mr. Weiner, what's your submission on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We have been using looting from the start. I think it is a situation of looting. If you like, I can use theft, theft of property instead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, is it some point you want to make a submission on?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If it may please the Court, I would just like an explanation. The point which Mr. Lukic was making is that, in fact, nobody brought this during the cross-examination. That is why Mr. Lukic was asking the our colleagues to say whether it was brought in the cross-examination, because according to the Defence teams over here, nobody brought these questions about the looting of the property or whatever during the cross-examination. And that was the point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. He didn't make it clear. It wasn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is why I wanted to assist the Trial Chamber. Because I saw that it was a misunderstanding. Mr. Lukic brought this up asking the Prosecutor to say who out of the Defence teams particularly put these questions to the witness during the cross-examination, because according to our knowledge, they were not put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Then that is clearer, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Also, Your Honour, if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- maybe an appropriate term would be a "seizure," because the other approach to this matter might be that during the war, there are certain regulations, war regulations, where for example military command is absolutely entitled, according to the military law, to collect all goods in the area. So maybe the other term which could be a seizure or collection or something like that, would be appropriate. More appropriate. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. I think the point being made here is that it's a matter which is going to be decided by the Trial Chamber whether or not anybody had the authority to collect the goods, clear the homes or the houses and that sort of thing, so that when you question the witness, make it a neutral term.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll use seizure. With regard to the other issue, Your Honour, Mr. Lukic brought up the matter of where the goods were taken, and he tried to raise an impression with the witness that it was brought -- the goods were brought to refugees thereafter. And I would just like to talk about Bosanski Samac where this gentleman was from and ask him who received the goods and let him tell you about -- let him tell the Court about how these goods were, in fact, distributed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, my questions referred only to firewood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: My view was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you check the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll move on while we find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you leave that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very quickly, sir, yesterday, the name Pero Pita was mentioned by Mr. Zecevic just about at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that the mentally handicapped gentleman from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, also yesterday, you were shown an exhibit, a notice to report for military service. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was apparently the second notice that you had received?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many notices had you received to report for military service?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for what army did you receive the notices?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, who was the army of Republika Srpska fighting?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what ethnic group, are you, sir?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you want to fight against your own people, sir?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't want to fight at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour. Your Honour, I don't have it at this time. I can go back to my office. The easiest thing I can say is he raised the issue of refugees. Mr. Pantelic also raised the issue of refugees, and they also raised the issue of looting, and I felt that they left the impression that the matters that were looted or seized or however you want to refer to it were taken to the refugees, and that's all I wanted to clear up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic's point was the reference to property being taken, rightly or wrongly, was only to firewood, as raised in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Then I would refer to that. May I at least have the right ask the witness who got the firewood back in Bosanski Samac, was it the refugees or the local citizens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, the persons who received the firewood in Bosanski Samac that you seized from other villages and other municipalities, who were they?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were ethnic Serbs. I drove firewood to shops and to those women up there, and I remember now they had lived in Samac for a long time. They were two sisters. One was called Mara, and I don't know the other's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me just one more thing, if I may say something about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About this seizure, as they call it, for the benefit of the refugees, I went to the house of Tovarice when you are going in the direction of Tisina, it's the first house on the left after the bridge. That man was living in his own house. He was not a refugee and I brought him a complete irrigation system, complete with a pump and engine. That is just one small detail, one of the many things that I delivered to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this person who received this property, the seized property, was this person a refugee without any property?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, on page 7001 -- actually it starts at page 7.000:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When leaving, when going and taking, removing property from family homes, did the -- were the owners present there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion was it abandoned property? Then there was an objection regarding to the objectionable -- we got into a difference of opinion on that, and you told us to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, so the term used was "property."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And then it continues. The property question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "The property that you were removing, that you were taking, was it usually most frequently given to refugees and the persons who had no property whatsoever? And the witness then asked, "Are you talking about Samac or Dubica?" And he said "Dubica." I just want to show the rest in Samac where he is familiar with his neighbours, who got the property.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So it's also inclusive, because property includes furniture.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let's go back to the property matter. The property which was seized from the houses, the furniture, the appliances, the electrical appliances that was brought back to Bosanski Samac, who received this property?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most of it was given to Rada, called Rada Specijalka, the mother of Mile Pancir. I took most of this to her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than Mile Pancir's mother, did you ever bring property to a home, any furniture to a home, that had a large number of similar-type property there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I moved a family who lived close in proximity to Mebos where there was a restaurant. That man was living along the gate of Mebos. The owner of the building rented two homes. Well, I helped to move him to an apartment building in proximity of the retirement home. That was, I participated in that, and the other person, my school friend known as "the Chinese." I think they moved to the fourth floor. So I moved his belongings from those two rooms, of very poor quality, worn, rundown, and he moved into this apartment. I don't know to whom that belonged previously. Probably a Catholic, but I cannot say anything precise about that. But in that apartment, we found furniture which was much, much better than what he had. We were going up the stairs with his items, and this was exactly across the road from the retirement home. It was also a tall building of a few floors. That's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The seized property that you obtained, did you give it -- were you giving it to refugees?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the refugees, I don't know. I know -- I knew a few of these refugees, but I wasn't taking it to them. I knew all the people to whom I was taking the items with the exception of two or three people. But the refugees were mainly housed in the buildings and apartments and homes which were already furnished. The home of my father was then a refugee lived in that apartment which was completely furnished. Everything remained in these apartments. It's only the owners who left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the home of your father, was that when he was removed from his home and sent to Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, did he give anyone permission to move into his home and use his furniture and other personal items?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, I would like just to for the record to file an objection to the -- I didn't raise it because I thought that it would -- I didn't want to interrupt my learned colleague, because I thought it would be maybe deemed as the abuse of my right, because we are objecting maybe too much. But it was quite inappropriate, quite inappropriate question concerning the mental state of one of the -- of one Pero Pita posed to this witness, because this witness is not an expert. And according to my knowledge, this Mr. Pero Pita, which the reference was made, is having a family and he is working normally, so I don't think that was a proper question from the Prosecutor's side posed to this witness about the mental health of a third person. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there has been previous testimony concerning this Pero Pita, and there was previous testimony that he had certain mental disabilities. And even in this testimony here, they said that he got a job, but they would never allow him to carry a gun which was consistent with the previous testimony that it was a mentally disabled person whose name was listed on a work list of some kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And the Trial Chamber obviously require a medical report if any finding was to be made, and it's the matter which the Defence can take up during their case. Because the what witness has stated is only limited to his own observation of the individual concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours. But it was not -- the way how the question was posed was -- it's in the transcript, it's page 9.11, until 9.13. The question was: "This Pero Pita, is this a mentally handicapped person?" And then the witness answered "yes." It was put to him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. Your objection it was a direct -- it was a leading question, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a leading question, moreover, and in my opinion, it was not appropriate. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Your objection is observed. You are through, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you very much for giving evidence to the Tribunal. We have now completed, and you may leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the meantime while the next witness is coming, I would like to report a problem with the display of the first monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which monitor?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This one in front of our Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And if the technical people can check during the break what is going on. When we want to have a video vision here, suddenly it is changed to transcript. We have numerous problems with that. We have to stand and then to disturb the trial proceedings. So we would kindly ask if the technical people can check that during the break what's going on with this monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You have your own monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but we are following the transcripts here, you know, with the PC and the official monitor. I mean, for the time being it's okay, but if during the break they can check that, it would be of assistance for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You just want to use that monitor for the video. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's all. And normally, it was okay until today. But probably something is happening. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You must understand that the people who control what is viewed have got their own rules which they comply with, all right. And that cannot be changed by the Trial Chamber unless it is occasioning some problem, some prejudice. And the point is in practice, you are entitled to only one monitor. You remember the question you raised on identification. I think it was yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So that monitor has to be controlled by the people responsible because nobody is using, whereas the monitor you are using is controlled by yourself. You can switch to the video, you can switch to the transcript. So you have no right actually to use two monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour. I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the next witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the meantime maybe we can follow our practice about the position of the defendants. They can swap up, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, they can swap before the witness is brought into the courtroom. Can the witness be taken outside for a moment. Just for a moment. Yes, the accused persons can switch places. They can switch. They know whoever sits where. That's fine. Thank you. The usher can now bring the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, please make your solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. Di FAZIO: Thank you. Examined by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your brother Esad Dagovic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same Esad Dagovic who gave evidence in this case some weeks ago?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just answer the next question with a yes or a no. Are you now residing in a European country?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You mean outside the Balkans? MR. Di FAZIO: Yes, I should have clarified that. Outside the Balkans and in a European country.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you living in a European country outside of the Balkans?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: In Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the remainder of your family born there?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many generations of Dagovics have lived in Bosanski Samac? I'm referring to your parents, grandparents, going back, and so on.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: A few generations. My parents, my grandparents. A few generations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you educated in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What level of education did you attain?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Secondary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perform military service in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you specialise in anything in particular during your year of military service?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you finished school, what sort of work did you do?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: I worked in a factory in Bosanski Samac as a tool mechanic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you do that for?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Approximately eight years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April of 1992, what sort of work were you doing?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: I was working in the private sector at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber what sort of work in the private sector you were doing. Just go into a bit more detail, please.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: I worked in a casino where we had poker slot machines and similar devices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it also be apt to describe this place as a games arcade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who owned this place?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Hasan Bicic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does he have a brother called Muhamed?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you friends with those two men?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about your brother Esad? Was he friends with them as well?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a member of any political party in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What party was that, and when did you join it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: The Party of Democrat Action, and I joined it in 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it fair to say that that party was aligned with the Muslim community in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in a certain sense, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you achieved any rank in the party as at April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was just an ordinary member of the SDA party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you served on any committees or taken part in any political activities on behalf the SDA?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you participated in any military activity organised on behalf the SDA?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your brother a member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about your father?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If asked how to describe your ethnic background, what would you say?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Bosniak. MR. Di FAZIO: Could the witness be shown D14/4 ter ID, please. This document, I believe, if Your Honours please, has not been translated yet. It's a Defence document, so I'll just ask the -- I think it's fairly easy to understand. It's just the title, and I'll ask the witness to run through the title of the document. May I see the original itself just before it's given to the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's a Defence document. Why hasn't it been translated yet? MR. Di FAZIO: It may have been, but I don't think the Prosecution has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe the Defence counsel concerned --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I can confirm that it has been translated, and I can provide the Court, Trial Chamber with the translation, official translation during the break. We were just waiting for an appropriate moment to bring the translation of this document. We didn't expect that this is going to be tendered today by the Prosecution. But we do have an official translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have it then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't have it here. It is actually in the Defence counsel room in our locker. So during the break, we will bring it here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll have it after the break. MR. Di FAZIO: I don't think it will trouble the Chamber much. It really consists of a list and the heading at the top, and once I get the heading translated, the rest is just names. So it shouldn't bother us unduly

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. You can proceed then. MR. Di FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you please read out the heading of this document, the first page.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: A list of self-organised inhabitants of Bosanski Samac engaged in the defence of the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe you've already had an opportunity outside of the courtroom to cast your eye through the names on this list. Have you not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what ethnic background the majority of the names are.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. Go to 154 and 156, and you see the name Safet Dagovic and Esad Dagovic, and next to that Pere Bosica. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume that's you and your brother, and that Pere Bosica is the street that your family used to live in in April 1992. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to who created this document or as to why your name and your brother's name appear in it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, those are two distinct questions, and the answers to both are important. MR. Di FAZIO: I'll split it in two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, please. MR. Di FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea who made that document, how it came into being?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea why your names, that is your name and your brother's name appear in the document?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until you arrived in The Hague to give evidence, had you ever seen that document before?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No. I'm seeing it now for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm finished with the document. Do you know a gentleman named Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how long would you say that you have known him?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: A few years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe your relationship with him. Was it a close one, one of acquaintances, or did you just know him by sight?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: I knew him just by sight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look around the courtroom, see if you can pick him out. If you can, identify him.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: The gentleman in a blue suit, a blue tie, and a beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Approximately as long as Mr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him when you went to school?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but only for a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any connection with your school?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: While I was attending the secondary school, Mr. Tadic was teaching me one of the subjects.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look around the courtroom and go through the same exercise again. See if you can identify him.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: The gentleman sitting in the middle with a moustache and glasses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know a gentleman named Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Some years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you comment on your relationship with him? Was it a close one, one of mere acquaintances, or did you just know him by sight?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: I knew him just by sight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: See if you can identify him.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: The third gentleman with grey hair, glasses, and sitting. MR. Di FAZIO: If Your Honours please, can the record reflect that the witness has correctly identified those three defendants, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. Di FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a man named Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, approximately as long as the other gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Think back to 1992, about how long would you say you had known him then?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: You're thinking before the war, the period before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: A few years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Think of it in this way: Would you say that you knew him when you were a child? Would you say you knew him when you were a teenager, or would you say you got to know of him when you became an adult?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: When I became an adult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And prior to the 16th of April, 1992, did you own or possess any weapons?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to the 16th of April, 1992, had you engaged in any patrols organised by any body or organ, patrols that were operating in the Bosanski Samac area?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to take you to the events of the night of the 16th and 17th. But perhaps before I do, I should ask you a few more questions about weapons. Did your brother own any weapons?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of weapon did he own?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: He had a pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about your father? Did he have any sort of weapon?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. Now, let's go to the night of the 16th and 17th of April. Were you in Bosanski Samac on that night?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear any disturbances or -- yes, did you hear any disturbances during the evening?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I could hear the shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did that start?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: At night, from the 16th to the 17th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know what was going on?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attempt to find out what was going on?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: I was afraid. I didn't know what was going on. We could hear a lot of strong shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The following morning, that is, the morning of the 17th, did you ascertain what had been happening during the night?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: On the 17th, I went, I left to go to work. And I saw that the military were moving around the town, and then I returned home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of military did you see?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: They were members of the 4th Detachment, and there were soldiers wearing camouflage uniforms and grey olive drab uniforms. I didn't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people who you saw in the 4th Detachment on the 17th, were those people who were obviously known to you, local people, people from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stay at home when you returned there?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout the remainder of the 17th, was there any sort of military activity around your house or in the street outside your house or in the area of Bosanski Samac in which you lived?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: There was, in a part of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that part of Bosanski Samac close to where you lived, or was that somewhere more distant from your home?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: More distant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually see what was happening there, or was it something that you heard about or was informed of?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: We heard gunfire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. Did you stay at home on the night of the 17th?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to turn your attention to the events on the following day, the 18th of April. On the 18th of April, was your entire family at home?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And incidentally, your family consists in its entirety of you, your brother, and your parents, mother and your father?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything happen on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: On the 18th of April, members of the 4th Detachment came to my house and asked us to turn over our weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thinking back, would you say that they arrived in the morning or in the afternoon or in the evening of the 18th?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was around noon. It was daytime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see these 4th Detachment members in your street prior to their arriving at your house?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you see them? How were you able to see them?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Because all the houses in the vicinity of my own belonged to Muslims, and I saw them through my window going from one house to the next.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any Serbs living in the vicinity of your home?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say you saw them, the soldiers, going from house to house. Did they enter Muslim houses, that is, houses owned by members of the Muslim faith?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice if they entered homes owned by ethnic Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any apartment blocks close to your home?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was one apartment block.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that in relation to your home?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: On the right, looking from my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see it from your house?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it inhabited by both members of -- by both Muslims and Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice if members of the 4th Detachment went to that apartment block?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: They entered, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice if they went into the homes or the apartments, I should say, of the Muslims in that apartment block?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they entered Muslim apartments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber if they entered the apartments owned by Serbs in that particular apartment block?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you say that they eventually arrived at your house. Were they accompanied by any vehicles?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was a tank with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yours was a house, a free-standing house, not part of an apartment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it have like a little front yard?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it had a front yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many soldiers came to your house?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: About 10 to 15 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they do? Go through this slowly, and giving us the detail, please.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: When they came to the courtyard, they called my brother and myself out into the yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they want?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: They asked us to turn over our weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, my brother turned over his gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Gun or pistol? Was it a pistol, a hand weapon, a handgun?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: It was a pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were your parents there? That is, standing around, aware of what was going on?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Our parents were outside, that is, they had come outside, but they told them to go back inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told them to go back inside?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Those soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the soldiers armed?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Heavily armed?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They had automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the armoured vehicle or tank or whatever it was in relation to your house?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: The tank was in the street headed -- that is, facing my front yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that these soldiers were members of the 4th Detachment. Were they local men, men from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice if any of the defendants were amongst them?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who? Which ones? Which defendants were there?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tadic and Mr. Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: They were standing on top of the tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric was wearing a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he armed?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Mr. Tadic? Tell the Chamber how he was dressed.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tadic was also wearing a camouflage uniform and a leather raincoat on top of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour leather raincoat?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: I can't really remember the colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of beard?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: A short beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Full beard?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a full beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he doing?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: He was also standing on top of the tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was any member of this group of soldiers, including both of these defendants that you've mentioned, apparently giving orders to the others, or apparently in command or apparently in some sort of senior position?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I could conclude, Mr. Zaric and Mr. Tadic were occupying some sort of commanding positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anyone else up on the tank with them, or just those two?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were other soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, there may have been other soldiers. But were there any other soldiers up on the tank?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was not just Mr. Tadic and Mr. Zaric who were up on the tank, but there were other soldiers as well in that position?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all of the soldiers there, all of them, local men?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What makes you say that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm saying that because there were soldiers among them who were from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why do you say that? Why do you say that they were from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: You could tell by the accent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Fadil Topcagic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he there?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Goran Buzakovic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he there?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: ... they were both local people from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your house searched?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you there when the people were searching the place?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: I was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they looking for?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: They were looking for weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone take the time to explain to you why they had come to your house with an armoured car and armed men, why they seized your weapons, why they were searching your house?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No, nobody explained the reason for the visit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the men, soldiers, including the defendants, eventually leave?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they eventually left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the unpleasantness of having armed men come to your home, were you or your family mistreated in any way? On this occasion, I mean.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't mistreat us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the following days, the days following the 18th, did you have an opportunity to listen to the radio?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a source of information as to what was going on in your community?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What had it been called prior to the 16th of April, this radio station?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Radio Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the days and weeks and months following the 16th and 17th of April, what was it called?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Serb Radio Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, did you listen to the radios fairly closely in the days following the 18th?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I listened. Not very often, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and the rest of the population of Bosanski Samac receive any sort of instructions over the radio?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find on occasions in the ensuing days and weeks that you had to go out of your house and out into the streets?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: I did have occasion, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have to wear anything in particular?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you have to wear in particular?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: We had to wear a white armband on our left arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to you give the Trial Chamber details about this. Who had to wear the white armband and where did you first hear of this requirement?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Those white armbands had to be worn by all Muslims and Croats in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the ensuing weeks and months, did you wear white armbands when you went out?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you first hear about this requirement of having to wear white armbands?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: The first time, I heard about it on the radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And doing the best you can, how long after the events of the 16th and 17th of April would you say that you first heard that? Matter of months or weeks or days?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps a couple of weeks after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go back to work in the games arcade that you had been working at prior to the 16th and 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't go back there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find that events took a turn that caused you to be doing work in the ensuing months after April 1992?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to tell the Chamber about that. First of all, when did you hear for the first time that you would be doing work in the next few months?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: A courier came for me, to my home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did the courier tell you?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: That I had to report to the building of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And doing the best you can, about how long after the 16th and 17th of April was that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Two weeks later roughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, report to the TO building?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your brother go with you?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The courier who came and told you, what ethnic background was he?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Uniformed?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Armed or unarmed?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: He didn't have a weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, apart from the courier, did you ever hear of the necessity to report there through any other means?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber what you saw when you reported.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: In the yard of the Territorial Defence, there were a lot of Croats and Muslims standing and wondering what was going to happen to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And did anyone inform them as to what was going to happen?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They informed us we had to go and do forced labour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who informed you that? Can you recall?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, if the person who informed you was a local person, or was it a stranger from somewhere else in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: He was a local.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you provided with any details as to how to start going about this work?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did this whole encounter take at the TO? Were you there for a matter of minutes or hours?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: We were there for about 40, 45 minutes perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, start to perform work following that visit to the TO?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps the very next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you perform this, to use your term, "forced labour"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I think it is not appropriate for my learned friend Mr. Di Fazio to use the term of one layperson which is strictly legal. So please, I ask my learned friend to avoid --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I think let's solve this problem this way: The Prosecution will be allowed to use the word "forced labour," whatever it means, but they know that they have to prove all the elements that are required be proved for the Trial Chamber to make such a finding.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So I'll allow them to use that term loosely, that's all. They know what they have to prove.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's your decision. I concur with it. Thank you, Your Honour. MR. Di FAZIO: With respect, this isn't a jury trial, and you are the judges of fact and, with respect, you know very well what the Prosecution has to prove. It is not it would be unthinkable that the Chamber would be swayed by the use of terms rather than facts, so I don't think it's a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, very well. That's the point I was trying to make to Mr. Pantelic. Please proceed. MR. Di FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how long did you perform this forced labour? Through about 1992, now. I just want you to give the Chamber an overall picture of your movements over the next few years before I start to look at the events in detail. So how long in 1992 did you perform forced labour? Until when?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: From April 1992 until December 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what happened in December of 1992? Not in detail, just tell us what change there was.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: In December 1992, I was mobilised by force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that into an army?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which army?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: The Serb army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you mobilised by force into that army?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Until December 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you eventually get out of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: In August 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that through -- did you go to Belgrade with the assistance of someone and eventually make your way through to the rest of Europe?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, first I went to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like to look at the events from April 1992 to December of 1992, the period of time in which you were performing what you refer to as "forced labour." First of all, you say that you engaged -- started upon this very soon after the meeting at the TO. How were you informed of whatever your assignment was?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: A courier would come for me and take me wherever I was supposed to work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did that system go on for, that is, the system using the courier, taking you to your work location?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: It didn't last for long, perhaps about a month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And thereafter, what system was used to get you to your workplace?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: First we had to report to the retirement home. That was an assembly point, and then they would transport us to town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. On the second system that you just described, who would report to the retirement home, first of all?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: All Muslims and Croats who had this forced labour thing had to report there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. MR. Di FAZIO: Would that be an appropriate time, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we'll take our break and resume the proceedings at 16.15 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. You just want to inform the Trial Chamber that I have provided the colleagues from the OTP with the English translation of the Document D14/4 ter ID. Also I gave to the Registry a number of copies for the Bench, and I believe that I'm going to need the number for this English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And then I would like to have an evidence number instead of ID number, because we will use these documents on many other occasions with some other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I notice that only the top part has been translated into English. Is it because the names -- the one in Serbo-Croat, the names --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The names haven't been translated because it contains all the names and addresses with name of the streets and numbers. So this is the official translation that we have received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. There are no annotations at all against any names?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So this one has to be used in conjunction with the ter one. So we can just have the formal number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. May I just inquire whether this is to be admitted into evidence as requested by counsel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any objection? MR. Di FAZIO: It could just be given a full exhibit number rather than ID number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honours. The B/C/S version is D14/4 ter, and English translation is D14/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, that's okay. We can proceed with examination-in-chief. MR. Di FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before the break, we were moving into the area of the forced labour that you performed throughout 1992. And you've told us of the two methods that were used to direct you to your location, namely the arrival of a courier who told you where to go, or assembling in front of the pensioners' hall and then getting the directions. There's just a few more details that I want to know about the pensioners' hall. First of all, where was it located?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: In Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the ensuing months, did you find yourself gathering there in the mornings?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of numbers of people would be gathered there waiting to receive their assignments?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, quite a number of people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do your best. Try and give us a figure. Are we talking about 20 or 30 people, 15.000 people? What sort of numbers?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Approximately 50, 60 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Men and women?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, women were also present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time would you gather in front of the pensioners' hall?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Early in the morning, approximately 7.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Once everyone had gathered, what would happen?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Then we would wait, depending on where we were to go and work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Presumably, not everyone who was gathered would go to the same location. Presumably, the assembly would then be split up and different groups would go to different jobs. Am I correct in saying that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how would the different groups be formed and how would they be told where to go?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it depended on the assignment, depended on the location of the assignment. There were the usual soldiers who would come out, and they would say, "You, you, and you go with me." And then we would board the trucks, and we would be taken there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And would this scene be repeated every day?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Saturdays and Sundays?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of trucks would you get into? Were they covered trucks or open trucks?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: They were covered trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you accompanied by a guard?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were accompanied by guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Armed guards?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go back to the assembly in the morning before you would set off for your particular task. Presumably, there would be more than one armed guard going around directing people to which particular task they had to perform.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There were two or three of them there. It depended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long would it take for the assembled people to be given their instructions for them to disperse off to their tasks? Was it matter that would take two or three minutes, or would it take 15 minutes, half an hour? What sort of time?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, approximately 5 to 10 minutes. It didn't last long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On these occasions when you assembled there, together with your fellow workers, did you ever see any of the defendants?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on occasion I did see Mr. Zaric and Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time of the morning, 8.00 or thereabouts, were there many other people around the street and around the pensioner hall, or did your group stand out?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: There weren't many people in the street. Practically we were the only ones there standing and waiting for the assignments to be allotted to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the occasions that you saw either Mr. Zaric or Mr. Tadic, what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: They were entering the building of the pensioners' hall. But what were they doing there, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The hall in front of which you were assembled, the same hall. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just try and give the Chamber now a list of the types of work that you did and the locations that you performed them at. And do it as best you can in chronological order. Once you've provided the Chamber that list, I'll ask you some more detailed questions about those particular jobs. Start at the beginning and try and finish at the end.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC
utterances.text: My first job was work performed at the silo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Second job, third job, and please continue.
